items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Samson never did drum with me, but he was around at gigs and everything

ctx.x: Anyway, he told the booker, I've had it, I just can't put my job up against a whiskey head, I'm going; that's the man that you're featuring, you don't know what condition he's going to be in; so he left.

So I took Salva Sanders then in the band. Another band that came in there was the Texas Rangers and a youngster, Pee Wee Wiley was the vocalist there, he had a voice, he could sing. See, Roy then, when this came up, things had got pretty tough around and somebody, I think it was a drummer, Samson Pratt (phonetic spelling), Samson never did drum with me, but he was around at gigs and everything, and somebody contacted Samson-- let's go to California. So Roy said to me, me and Samson are going to California and…

Roy had a car--he had made a little money and had married a girl in Tulsa that had this average job and was doing pretty good and he had a car, and he told the boys that we'll just pay for the gas and we'll go out to California and I believe we'll do better than we're doing now.
